chief_complaint: Advanced chronic kidney disease (stage 4) with preparation for kidney transplantation and associated comorbidities (diabetes, hypertension, anemia).
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 62‑year‑old Black male with a 30‑year history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension. Over time he progressed from microalbuminuria (1994) to proteinuria (2007) and sequential CKD stages 1‑4, reaching stage 4 in 2011. He is currently listed as awaiting kidney transplantation. Diabetes is treated with a mixed‑insulin regimen, but the most recent HbA1c of 4.0% suggests possible overtreatment. Hypertension is managed with low‑dose lisinopril and hydrochlorothiazide, though blood pressure values are unavailable. He has anemia of chronic disease, metabolic syndrome, hypertriglyceridemia, obesity (BMI ≥ 30), diabetic neuropathy, and osteoarthritis of the knee for which he takes naproxen, a medication contraindicated in advanced CKD. He reports ongoing stress and maintains full‑time employment. No recent lipid panel, eGFR, or blood pressure measurements are recorded.
